title: Importing Epidemiological Contact Tracing Models to Vulnerability Spread Analysis

original_idea.body:
# Importing Epidemiological Contact Tracing Models to Vulnerability Spread Analysis

**Problem:** Vulnerabilities in shared libraries (e.g., Log4Shell) spread through dependency graphs in ways analogous to infectious disease. AI tools could assist in predicting spread, but no such application has been formalized.

**Direction:** Model a dependency graph (using a public dataset like libraries.io or SBOM data) as a contact network. Apply SIR-style epidemic models to predict how a newly discovered vulnerability propagates through dependent packages. Evaluate whether AI-predicted vulnerability likelihood correlates with actual CVE propagation patterns.

**Why it matters:** Rapid response to supply chain vulnerabilities requires knowing which packages are likely affected before manual review is complete. An epidemic-inspired model could prioritize AI scanning resources.

**Relevant context:** Supply chain attacks doubled in 2025 (Bastion 2026 report). LiteLLM supply chain compromise (Trend Micro 2026). Epidemiological methods applied to vulnerability propagation is unexplored.
